hook: Chelsea Finn is a computer scientist working at the intersection of robotics and machine learning. She earned a BS in electrical engineering and computer science from MIT, then a PhD in computer science from UC Berkeley, where she helped develop Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML), a widely used algorithm for training models that adapt quickly to new tasks. She then worked as a researcher across Google's Brain and DeepMind teams before becoming an Assistant Professor of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering at Stanford University. There she leads the IRIS Lab, which studies how robots and other agents can develop broadly intelligent behavior through learning and interaction. More recently, she co-founded Physical Intelligence, a startup building general-purpose foundation models for robots. Her work has earned the ACM Doctoral Dissertation Award, an ONR Young Investigator Award, and a Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers.
